headline: AUSTRALIA BREAKS RARE EARTH GROUND — ARAFURA NOLANS 4,440 TPa NdPr, HYUNDAI, KIA AND GOVT OFFTAKE SECURED
snippet: Arafura Rare Earths (ASX: ARU) has commenced construction at Nolans Bore in Australia's Northern Territory — the country's first fully integrated rare earth ore-to-oxide operation — targeting 4,440 metric tonnes of NdPr oxide annually over a 38-year mine life. The Australian government is purchasing up to 500 tonnes per year via its Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve, with Hyundai, Kia, Siemens Gamesa, and Traxys holding additional offtake; project financing closes October 2026 and production commissioning is targeted for late 2029.

headline: DRC COBALT QUOTA LOCKS IN STRUCTURAL SHORTAGE — HYDROXIDE $26/LB (UP 350%) AS IEA FLAGS DEFICIT THROUGH 2035
snippet: The DRC's 96,600-tonne annual cobalt export quota — roughly half 2024 export levels — remains in force through 2027, creating a structural deficit Fastmarkets projects at 10,700 tonnes minimum and up to 80,000 tonnes (27% of global demand) if the ceiling is strictly enforced. Cobalt hydroxide has hit $25.90–$26.00 per pound, a 350% premium over its February 2025 trough of $5.60–$5.75, while the IEA confirms the cobalt market is shifting into structural deficit starting 2026 with the supply gap widening from roughly 15% to over 25%.

headline: RING OF FIRE COPPER-NICKEL RESTARTS: PTX METALS 5,000M W2 PROGRAM BACK AFTER FIRST NATIONS ACCORD
snippet: PTX Metals (TSX-V: PTX) has resumed a 5,000-metre diamond drilling program at its W2 Copper-Nickel-PGE-Gold project in Ontario's Ring of Fire, focusing on the CA1 Zone in the underexplored Central area following a seven-month pause for First Nations consultations. A July 10 community meeting — where PTX addressed environmental protocols and employment opportunities — unlocked resumption of drilling and a concurrent soil sampling and prospecting program across T-Target, Lake Rowell, and North Limb areas.

headline: TALISKER BRALORNE-MUSTANG: 4,884 OZ AU AT 7.99 G/T THROUGH AUGUST — PHASE 3 BRALORNE WEST LATERAL UNDERWAY
snippet: Talisker Resources (TSX: TSK) reported 4,884 ounces of gold produced and 5,558 ounces sold through August 31 at its Bralorne-Mustang mine in British Columbia, with 26,730 metres of resource conversion drilling completed across the Mustang Main Zone and developing Bralorne West Zone. Phase 3 lateral development toward the Bralorne West Zone centre commenced September 3; the company has invested $13.4 million in 2026 capital including a new 32-bed accommodation facility and a ventilation upgrade commissioning in late October.

headline: IRVING RESOURCES DEPLOYS 4-RIG ASSAULT ON OKU GOLD-SILVER — HIGH-GRADE HOKKAIDO FEEDER PERMITS FILED
snippet: Irving Resources (CSE: IRV) has four diamond drill rigs active at its Omu gold-silver project in Hokkaido, Japan: one testing Nanko silica-rich targets, two running a JX/Irving collaboration at the Honpi zone, and a fourth drilling extensions of the Omu Sinter deposit. Previous drilling at Nanko returned 47.7 metres at 0.98 g/t Au and 68.96 g/t Ag — including 1.05 metres at 10.68 g/t Au and 187.81 g/t Ag — and Irving has now filed permits for deeper feeder hole targets below the known mineralization.

headline: SUMITOMO BACKS $2.3M FIRST DRILL AT INOMIN'S BEAVER-LYNX — 3,453M AT ONUKI BESIDE GIBRALTAR MINE
snippet: Inomin Mines (TSX-V: MINE) has completed the $2.3 million Beaver-Lynx polymetallic exploration program in south-central British Columbia — the largest single investment in the project and the first-ever drilling at the Lynx block, fully funded by Sumitomo Metal Mining Canada Ltd. Nine holes totalling 3,452.8 metres at the Onuki zone, a 6 km² magnetic anomaly adjacent to the Gibraltar mine (Canada's second-largest open-pit copper operation), are awaiting assay; management says Onuki displays characteristics similar to the producing Beaver zone.

headline: IEA 2026: COPPER DEFICIT NARROWS TO 25% BUT PERSISTS TO 2035 — COBALT GAP WIDENS, CHINA OWNS THE CHOKEPOINTS
snippet: The IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 finds the copper supply deficit has narrowed from 30% to 25% based on the current project pipeline but persists through 2035, with the lithium outlook showing a similar marginal improvement. Cobalt's position has worsened — the projected supply gap widened from roughly 15% to over 25% as DRC export quotas take effect — and a common thread runs through all projections: China dominates the refining and processing stage for copper, lithium, cobalt, and rare earths, creating systemic concentration risk.

headline: URANIUM MINERS UP 17-21% IN SEPTEMBER — NORTHSHORE INDEX LAPS SPOT AS SUPPLY DISRUPTIONS FORCE EQUITY REPRICING
snippet: Uranium equity ETFs are posting one of the sector's strongest months, with the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index up 17.01% and junior uranium miners up 21.75% in September — significantly outpacing spot uranium's recovery to near $90/lb. Sprott's September uranium report attributes the re-rating to supply disruptions at Cameco's Cigar Lake and McArthur River operations, Kazatomprom's reagent constraints, and accelerating utility buying as the 38-nation nuclear expansion pledge translates into real procurement decisions.

headline: GOLD MINER MARGINS HIT $3,076/OZ IN Q1 — RECORD FCF DISCONNECTS FROM EQUITY MULTIPLES HEADING INTO FOMC WEEK
snippet: Gold mining companies generated average all-in sustaining cost margins of $3,076 per ounce in Q1 2026 — a 134% year-over-year increase — yet major producers trade at valuation multiples well below historical peaks despite generating record free cash flow. With AISC industry-wide below $2,000 per ounce and gold holding above $4,300 through the current correction, the cash is flowing toward dividends, buybacks, and royalty investments rather than triggering the share price re-rating analysts argue is overdue.
